docRequirement: authentication.md:168 (§ Authentication precedence, list item 1) binds the top precedence tier to three named toggles: "Cloud provider credentials, when `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX`, or `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY` is set." Any one of those three, present in the environment of the `claude` process, outranks `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` (tier 2), `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (tier 3), `apiKeyHelper` (4), `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (5) and the `/login` subscription (6). The page's only exception (:175) is a signed-in Claude apps gateway session, which we do not ship. Nessy's own invariant — stated verbatim at packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:257 and packages/shared/AGENTS.md — is that this tier must not be reachable from the Claude SDK path at all, so the doc's enumeration is the exact list our strip must cover.
current: The Claude SDK subprocess env inherits the host's whole environment and then removes exactly one of the three named toggles. packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:239-245 builds it as `{...process.env, ...getProxyEnvVars(), ...envOverrides, NESSY_DEBUG}`; :257-262 deletes `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`, `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL` under the comment "Bedrock must never be routed through the Claude SDK path." A second, independently hand-maintained copy of the same list is packages/shared/src/config/llm-connections.ts:931-935 (`CLAUDE_BEDROCK_ROUTING_ENV_KEYS`), cleared from the host `process.env` by `clearClaudeBedrockRoutingEnvVars` (llm-connections.ts:969-975) at packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:917, in the `postInit` "clean state" block that otherwise deletes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` (claude-agent.ts:914-916) before `resolveAuthEnvVars` writes the connection's own credential (claude-agent.ts:921-930, llm-connections.ts:1021-1076). `grep -rna` (NUL-safe) over apps/*/src, packages/*/src and scripts finds `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX` in exactly one place — packages/shared/src/config/managed-env.ts:126, the managed-settings withheld-env classifier, a different subsystem that strips nothing here — and `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY` in no source file at all. `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, precedence tier 2 and therefore above the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` postInit does set, is likewise absent from the whole Claude path (only managed-env.ts:141). The ambient values really arrive: on packaged macOS, apps/electron/src/main/shell-env.ts:28-77 runs `$SHELL -l -i -c env` and copies every variable into `process.env`, skipping only `VITE_`-prefixed keys. And the runtime we spawn really reads them: `grep -ao 'CLAUDE_CODE_USE_[A-Z_]*' node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.mjs` returns ANTHROPIC_AWS, BEDROCK, COWORK_PLUGINS, FOUNDRY, MANTLE, VERTEX. `resetManagedAnthropicAuthEnvVars` (llm-connections.ts:977-990, called from packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:7522) restores from `MANAGED_ANTHROPIC_AUTH_ENV_KEYS` (llm-connections.ts:941-950), which spreads the same three-key Bedrock list, so it leaves the other toggles alone too.
divergence: The mechanism is right and the coverage is short. We enforce "no cloud-provider tier on the Claude SDK path" for `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` and omit `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX` and `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY` — two of the three names the doc's tier-1 sentence lists. No value or key name is misspelled; two entries are simply missing from two hand-copied lists (options.ts:260-262 and llm-connections.ts:931-935), and the duplication is why they drifted. Two adjacent gaps share the same root cause and the same two sites: the shipped SDK 0.3.183 also branches on `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS` and `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE` (the latter is finding f116, so f116 and f118 are one edit), and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` — tier 2, above the API key we do set — is stripped nowhere. Not a recorded owner decision: none of the nine dated decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 touches an env strip list, and shipping no Vertex/Foundry provider is the reason an ambient toggle is unwanted, not a reason to allow it.

change.what: Widen the constant at :931-935 to every cloud-provider routing toggle the shipped SDK branches on, and rename it to say so: `CLAUDE_CLOUD_PROVIDER_ROUTING_ENV_KEYS = ['CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK','CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX','CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY','CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS','CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE','AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK','ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL','ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL','CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH']` (the last three Mantle/Bedrock entries close f116 in the same edit). Rename `clearClaudeBedrockRoutingEnvVars` (:969-975) to `clearClaudeCloudProviderRoutingEnvVars` and update its two importers (claude-agent.ts:30, :917) plus the test import; keep the loop body unchanged. Carry the doc citation in the comment: authentication.md:168 names the three, the SDK bundle adds two more. `MANAGED_ANTHROPIC_AUTH_ENV_KEYS` (:941-950) spreads the constant, so the `MANAGED_ANTHROPIC_AUTH_ENV_BASELINE` at :959-967 forces the new keys to `undefined` automatically — that is the wanted behaviour for `resetManagedAnthropicAuthEnvVars`, no separate edit.

Replace the three hand-written `delete env.…` statements at :260-262 with a loop over the shared constant imported from ../config/llm-connections.ts (`for (const key of CLAUDE_CLOUD_PROVIDER_ROUTING_ENV_KEYS) delete env[key]`). This is the root-cause edit: the duplicate literal list is why Vertex/Foundry were missed in one place and not the other, and a single source makes the next SDK toggle a one-line change. Keep the existing comment's second sentence (generic `AWS_*` stays untouched) — it is still true, and check the import does not create a cycle (options.ts already imports from ../config/*; if it does, move the constant to a leaf module such as config/claude-env-keys.ts and re-export).

One line: add `delete process.env.ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN;` to the clean-state block at :914-916, next to `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. authentication.md:169 puts `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` at precedence tier 2, above the tier-3 `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` that :928-930 writes from the connection, so an ambient bearer token currently wins over the credential the session resolved. Update the renamed import at :30 and the call at :917 in the same edit.

blastRadius: Two independent consumers of the strip, both must widen: `buildClaudeSubprocessEnv` (options.ts:236) is called only by `getDefaultOptions` (options.ts:272), which is called from claude-agent.ts:1214, :3015, :3144 (the turn/subagent query paths), packages/shared/src/config/llm-validation.ts:67 (`validateAnthropicConnection`, reached from agent/diagnostics.ts:230, backend/factory.ts:902 and backend/internal/drivers/anthropic.ts:149 — connection-test surfaces that spawn the SDK with maxTurns:1) and packages/shared/src/validation/url-validator.ts:64 (`validateMcpUrl`, no non-test caller today). `clearClaudeBedrockRoutingEnvVars` has one production caller, claude-agent.ts:917; `MANAGED_ANTHROPIC_AUTH_ENV_KEYS` feeds `resetManagedAnthropicAuthEnvVars`, called from packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:7522, so widening the constant also widens what a connection switch resets in the host `process.env` — intended, but it is a host-global mutation shared by every live session in the process. Tests that pin the current narrow list: packages/shared/src/config/__tests__/llm-connections-auth-env.test.ts:9-14/:71-73/:86-88/:100-102, packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/claude-turn-options.test.ts:58-78, packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/workspace-claude-config-dir.test.ts:19/:75, packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/pi-agent-bedrock-env.test.ts:26/:47, packages/shared/src/config/__tests__/managed-env.test.ts:43-49. No wire, IPC or persistence boundary is crossed: nothing here is serialized to disk or over RPC — it is process-environment construction only, so this is NOT one of the repo's risk triggers. The upstream feeder is apps/electron/src/main/shell-env.ts:28-77 (packaged macOS login-shell import); leaving that filter alone is correct, the fix belongs at the Claude boundary. Reachability is gated by `NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE` (packages/shared/src/feature-flags.ts:142, default off per the flag table; backend/factory.ts:76 and backend/internal/runtime-resolver.ts:516 throw "Claude support is not included in this build." otherwise) — the same flag the existing Bedrock strip exists to protect.
userImpact: In a Claude-enabled build, a user whose shell exports `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX=1` or `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY=1` — common if the same machine also runs Claude Code against a corporate Vertex/Foundry deployment — selects their configured Anthropic connection in Nessy and sends a turn, and the SDK subprocess routes to that cloud provider instead, at the top precedence tier. With a complete ambient provider config (project/region/credentials) the swap is silent: the turn succeeds against the wrong account, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` from the connection is ignored so a custom-endpoint or Ollama card is bypassed, and no surface in the app names Vertex or Foundry. With a partial config the turn fails with a provider routing error that mentions no connection the user configured — and because the app never reads the variable, neither the error mapper (agent/claude-sdk-error-mapper.ts) nor a diagnostics run can attribute it. The same shell exporting `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` is already immune, which is exactly what makes this look like a Nessy bug rather than an environment one. Default builds have the Claude provider off, so nothing is observable there; enabling `NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE=1` at build time is what surfaces it. Separately, an ambient `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` outranks the API key postInit resolves, with the same silent-wrong-account outcome.
